key_insight: This paper tackles continual learning for robot policies by using world models to steer a frozen generalist policy across tasks without repeatedly rewriting the policy itself. The core idea is to preserve earlier skills while still adapting to new tasks, reducing catastrophic forgetting in sequential robot learning.
problem_solved: Generalist robot policies improve from reinforcement learning, but fine-tuning causes forgetting of prior tasks and steering-based methods can still shift forgetting into shared steering modules. This work addresses how to continually adapt robot policies to new tasks while retaining performance on earlier ones.
method: Use a frozen generative robot policy rather than fully fine-tuning policy weights for each new task.
Train or leverage a world model to provide task-aware steering signals that guide the policy during execution or adaptation.
Apply continual/ sequential task adaptation so the system can learn new behaviors while minimizing degradation on previously learned tasks.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a path toward more scalable robot learning systems that can keep improving over time without expensive retraining from scratch. It is especially relevant for long-horizon deployment settings where robots must handle new tasks while retaining old capabilities.

paper_title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models
paper_authors: Bahey Tharwat, Iman Nematollahi, Marvin Alles, Xingyuan Zhang, Akshay L Chandra
